d.d: Used as a tag question, to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said.
d.x: These hot dogs are pretty good, eh?

d.d: In isolation, a request for repetition or clarification of what has just been said.
d.x: —I've been studying Graphiurus murinus. —Eh? Studying what?

d.d: In isolation, expressing surprise or confusion.
d.x: —You're going to be a dad! —Eh? You're joking!

d.d: Used to negate the following verb; (am/are/is/do/does) not.
